segments.arabic: [352] حدثنا أبو عاصم عن مالك عن أبي الزناد عن عبد الرحمن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: لا يصلي أحدكم في الثوب الواحد ليس على عاتقيه شيء
segments.english: None of you should pray in a single garment with nothing on his shoulders.

notes: The selected عاتقيه is dual (both shoulders), as in the modern print. The historical print has the singular عاتقه in the report. Its attribution also says Messenger of Allah where the selected and modern text say Prophet. The selected wording remains unchanged; no legal ruling is appended.

segments.arabic: [353] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عكرمة قال: سمعته أو كنت سألته قال: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Ikrimah—he said, “I heard him, or I had asked him”—who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say:

segments.arabic: أشهد أني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: من صلى في ثوب واحد فليخالف بين طرفيه
segments.english: I testify that I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever prays in a single garment should cross its two ends.”

notes: The full chain retains سمعته أو كنت سألته, the uncertainty between hearing directly and having asked. Fath al-Bari identifies this as Yahya speaking about Ikrimah, not Ikrimah doubting whether he heard Abu Hurayrah. The English parenthesis belongs to that transmission. Neither the alternative wrote to me from other recensions nor an omitted certainty is substituted.

Both prints retain the uncertainty and Abu Hurayrah’s explicit testimony. Bewley and the Khan-family comparison abbreviate the earlier chain; the Khan-family body also omits the testimony. The instruction crosses the two ends; on his shoulders is not added from other recensions.

segments.arabic: [354] حدثنا يحيى بن صالح قال: حدثنا فليح بن سليمان عن سعيد بن الحارث قال
segments.english: Yahya ibn Salih related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith, who said:

segments.arabic: سألنا جابر بن عبد الله عن الصلاة في الثوب الواحد، فقال خرجت مع النبي ﷺ في بعض أسفاره فجئت ليلة لبعض أمري فوجدته يصلي وعلي ثوب واحد فاشتملت به وصليت إلى جانبه
segments.english: We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah about praying in a single garment. He said: I went out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on one of his journeys. One night I came on some business of mine and found him praying. I was wearing a single garment, so I wrapped myself in it and prayed beside him.

segments.arabic: فلما انصرف قال: ما السرى يا جابر فأخبرته بحاجتي فلما فرغت قال: ما هذا الاشتمال الذي رأيت قلت: كان ثوب يعني ضاق قال: فإن كان واسعا فالتحف به وإن كان ضيقا فاتزر به
segments.english: When he finished, he said: “What brings you out at night, Jabir?” I told him what I needed. When I had finished, he said: “What was this wrapping that I saw?” I said: “It was a garment”—meaning it was too narrow. He said: “If it is wide, wrap yourself in it; if it is narrow, wear it as an izar.”

notes: The selected and both printed witnesses say سألنا (we asked); the Khan-family comparison says I asked. The night-time force of السرى and the narrator’s يعني ضاق explanation remain. Fath al-Bari discusses the abbreviated كان ثوب phrase; the English retains it and its explanation separately rather than silently replacing the quotation.
Izar is the waist-wrapped garment, retained as the source term consistently with earlier Prayer reports. No named expedition, errand or additional posture detail from other versions is inserted.

segments.arabic: [355] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن سفيان قال: حدثني أبو حازم عن سهل قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abu Hazim related to me, from Sahl, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رجال يصلون مع النبي ﷺ عاقدي أزرهم على أعناقهم كهيئة الصبيان، ويقال للنساء لا ترفعن رؤوسكن حتى يستوي الرجال جلوسا
segments.english: Men used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with their izars tied around their necks like children. The women were told: “Do not raise your heads until the men are sitting upright.”

notes: The selected and historical print have the passive ويقال للنساء (the women were told); the modern print has وقال للنساء. The Khan-family comparison explicitly attributes the instruction to the Prophet. The selected passive remains without an invented speaker. Fath al-Bari records this reading and alternative attributions separately.

The selected Sahl is not expanded to Sahl ibn Sad, although the historical print gives that longer name. Their necks, the comparison with children and the condition until the men sit upright remain; no explanation of the prohibition is appended.

segments.arabic: [356] حدثنا يحيى قال: حدثنا أبو معاوية عن الأعمش عن مسلم عن مسروق عن مغيرة بن شعبة قال:
segments.english: Yahya related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت مع النبي ﷺ في سفر، فقال: يا مغيرة خذ الإداوة فأخذتها فانطلق رسول الله ﷺ حتى توارى عني فقضى حاجته وعليه جبة شأمية فذهب ليخرج يده من كمها فضاقت فأخرج يده من أسفلها فصببت عليه فتوضأ وضوءه للصلاة ومسح على خفيه ثم صلى
segments.english: I was with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. He said: “Mughirah, take the water vessel.” I took it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went away until he was out of my sight and relieved himself. He was wearing a Syrian robe. He tried to bring his hand out of its sleeve, but it was too tight, so he brought his hand out from underneath it. I poured water for him, and he performed ablution as he did for prayer, wiped over his leather socks, and then prayed.

notes: Both Arabic prints retain the complete chain, Syrian jubbah, hand in the singular, narrow sleeve, hand brought out from below, ablution, wiping and prayer. The Khan-family comparison uses plural hands. The selected singular remains. Robe is a provisional English garment rendering; leather socks follows the existing reader terminology.

segments.arabic: [357] حدثنا مطر بن الفضل قال: حدثنا روح قال: حدثنا زكريا بن إسحاق حدثنا عمرو بن دينار قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله يحدث
segments.english: Matar ibn al-Fadl related to us. He said: Rawh related to us. He said: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq related to us; ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah relate:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان ينقل معهم الحجارة للكعبة وعليه إزاره، فقال له العباس عمه يا ابن أخي لو حللت إزارك فجعلت على منكبيك دون الحجارة قال: فحله فجعله على منكبيه فسقط مغشيا عليه فما رؤي بعد ذلك عريانا ﷺ
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was carrying stones with them for the Ka‘bah while wearing his izar. His uncle al-‘Abbas said to him: “Nephew, why not loosen your izar and put it on your shoulders beneath the stones?” He said: He loosened it and put it on his shoulders, then fell unconscious. He was not seen naked after that, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The complete Matar / Rawh / Zakariyya ibn Ishaq / Amr ibn Dinar / Jabir chain, nephew address, garment beneath the stones, fainting and final honorific remain. Both printed witnesses preserve the report; the historical print omits the closing honorific that appears in the selected source and modern print.

No age, city, construction detail, theological explanation or hidden continuation is added from comparisons. The pronoun in He said remains without assigning the intervening narrator more specifically than the source; Fath al-Bari notes the possible attribution.

segments.arabic: [358] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن محمد عن أبي هريرة قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: قام رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فسأله عن الصلاة في الثوب الواحد، فقال أو كلكم يجد ثوبين
segments.english: A man stood up before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about praying in a single garment. He said: “Can all of you find two garments?”

segments.arabic: ثم سأل رجل عمر، فقال إذا وسع الله فأوسعوا جمع رجل عليه ثيابه صلى رجل في إزار ورداء في إزار وقميص في إزار وقباء في سراويل ورداء في سراويل وقميص في سراويل وقباء في تبان وقباء في تبان وقميص قال وأحسبه قال في تبان ورداء
segments.english: Then a man asked ‘Umar, who said: “When Allah gives you abundance, make use of it. Let a man gather his garments about him. Let a man pray in an izar and a rida, in an izar and a shirt, in an izar and a qaba, in trousers and a rida, in trousers and a shirt, in trousers and a qaba, in a tubban and a qaba, in a tubban and a shirt.” He said: And I think he said: “In a tubban and a rida.”

notes: The clothing statement remains explicitly attributed to Umar, separate from the Prophetic answer. All eight stated pairs and the ninth uncertain pair remain in source order. The final I think he said is not converted into a certain ninth instruction. Fath al-Bari explains the past-tense forms as instructions; that is the provisional English rendering here.

Source terms are retained to avoid conflating historical garments: izar is a waist wrap, rida an upper wrap, qaba a coat, and tubban a brief lower garment without trouser legs. Shirt renders qamis; trousers renders sarawil. These descriptions are review notes, not inserted into the quotation. Fath al-Bari distinguishes the garments. No otherwise or additional condition from an English comparison is inserted.

segments.arabic: [359] حدثنا عاصم بن علي قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن الزهري عن سالم عن ابن عمر قال
segments.english: ‘Asim ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

segments.arabic: سأل رجل رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: ما يلبس المحرم، فقال لا يلبس القميص ولا السراويل ولا البرنس ولا ثوبا مسه الزعفران ولا ورس فمن لم يجد النعلين فليلبس الخفين وليقطعهما حتى يكونا أسفل من الكعبين
segments.english: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “What does a person in ihram wear?” He said: “He does not wear a shirt, trousers, a hooded cloak, or a garment touched by saffron or wars. Whoever cannot find sandals should wear leather socks and cut them so that they are below the ankles.”

segments.arabic: وعن نافع عن ابن عمر عن النبي ﷺ مثله
segments.english: And from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the same.

notes: The selected report, both prints and Bewley preserve the closing Nafi / Ibn Umar transmission. The matched Khan-family EPUB body omits it; it remains a separate complete chain segment. This is related content to selected 134 but its order and wording are not replaced by that earlier report.

The order saffron then wars, the two socks below the ankles, and the selected garments remain. Wars is a source dye term; no perfume explanation, turban from other recensions or further instruction is inserted.

segments.arabic: [360] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا ليث عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنه قال
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Layth related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said:

segments.arabic: نهى رسول الله ﷺ عن اشتمال الصماء وأن يحتبي الرجل في ثوب واحد ليس على فرجه منه شيء
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade wrapping oneself in the samma’ manner, and a man sitting with his knees drawn up, wrapped in a single garment, with none of it covering his private parts.

notes: The exact source term samma is retained in the working English. Fath al-Bari records different descriptions of this wrapping style; selecting one detailed explanation and making it part of the hadith would exceed the selected sentence. The English comparisons’ parenthetical explanations are not imported.

Ihtiba is rendered sitting with knees drawn up and wrapped in a garment, following the lexical description in Fath al-Bari. The explicit absence of covering over the private parts is retained here and is not silently copied into the shorter next report. No legal interpretation is appended.

segments.arabic: [361] حدثنا قبيصة بن عقبة قال: حدثنا سفيان عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة قال
segments.english: Qabisah ibn ‘Uqbah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: نهى النبي ﷺ عن بيعتين عن اللماس والنباذ وأن يشتمل الصماء وأن يحتبي الرجل في ثوب واحد
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two types of sale, limas and nibadh, and wrapping oneself in the samma’ manner, and a man sitting with his knees drawn up, wrapped in a single garment.

notes: The two named sales limas and nibadh remain source terms. They concern touching and throwing, but the comparisons’ descriptions of contract mechanics are commentary rather than wording of this selected report. Fath al-Bari identifies the terms and refers their explanation to the Book of Sales.

The repeated samma and ihtiba wording remains. Unlike 360, this report does not explicitly repeat the clause about uncovered private parts. That clause is not imported. Full Qabisah / Sufyan / Abu al-Zinad / al-Araj / Abu Hurayrah chain remains.

segments.arabic: [362] حدثنا إسحاق قال: حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا ابن أخي بن شهاب عن عمه قال: أخبرني حميد بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن أبا هريرة قال
segments.english: Ishaq related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: The nephew of Ibn Shihab related to us, from his uncle, who said: Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf informed me that Abu Hurayrah said:

segments.arabic: بعثني أبو بكر في تلك الحجة في مؤذنين يوم النحر نؤذن بمنى ألا لا يحج بعد العام مشرك ولا يطوف بالبيت عريان
segments.english: Abu Bakr sent me during that Hajj among those making proclamations on the Day of Sacrifice. We proclaimed at Mina: “Take notice: no polytheist is to perform Hajj after this year, and no one is to go around the House naked.”

segments.arabic: قال حميد بن عبد الرحمن ثم أردف رسول الله ﷺ عليا فأمره أن يؤذن ب براءة
segments.english: Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman said: Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent ‘Ali after them and instructed him to proclaim Bara’ah.

segments.arabic: قال أبو هريرة فأذن معنا علي في أهل منى يوم النحر لا يحج بعد العام مشرك ولا يطوف بالبيت عريان
segments.english: Abu Hurayrah said: ‘Ali proclaimed with us among the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice: “No polytheist is to perform Hajj after this year, and no one is to go around the House naked.”

notes: The full unnamed nephew-of-Ibn-Shihab relationship remains without supplying his personal name. Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman’s intervening attribution and Abu Hurayrah’s return to speaking remain distinct, unlike the compressed Khan-family account. Both printed witnesses retain those transitions.

The selected ألا attention particle is retained as Take notice; the historical print instead reads أن لا at this point. Fath al-Bari records the variant. The source title Baraah remains without silently replacing it with another surah title, supplying a verse range, or adding a date not in this report. Both full proclamations remain.

segments.arabic: [363] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثني ابن أبي الموالي عن محمد بن المنكدر قال
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibn Abi al-Mawali related to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said:

segments.arabic: دخلت على جابر بن عبد الله وهو يصلي في ثوب ملتحفا به ورداؤه موضوع فلما انصرف قلنا يا أبا عبد الله تصلي ورداؤك موضوع قال: نعم أحببت أن يراني الجهال مثلكم رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي هكذا
segments.english: I went in to Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah while he was praying wrapped in a garment, with his rida laid aside. When he finished, we said: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, do you pray with your rida laid aside?” He said: “Yes. I wanted ignorant people like you to see me. I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying like this.”

notes: The source changes from I went in to we said; both prints preserve this. The Khan-family comparison has I said and O Abdullah, while the selected and both prints have the plural and Abu Abd Allah. The selected wording remains.

The initial chain says Ibn Abi al-Mawali without an expanded personal name; the historical print reads related to us where the selected and modern print read related to me. Rida remains the source term for the upper wrap. No extra ruling or description is added.
